clauses.reason: EO 11767 designated the Organization of African Unity under the International Organizations Immunities Act in a single paragraph. Section 3 of EO 13377, signed April 13, 2005 and published at 70 FR 20263 on April 18, 2005, states: "Sec. 3. Revocation. Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked." The revocation names the order and has no delayed effective date or exception, so the clause ended on April 13, 2005, the signing date.

conflict_resolutions.NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW: The only current-law lead is the eCFR list at 8 CFR 316.20, which still names the Organization of African Unity designation; it is a stale list entry and not a current legal predicate that keeps this order in force, because section 3 of EO 13377 (70 FR 20263) states 'Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked.' The packet's status for the order stays no, and the first end is that revocation.

research_rationale:
EO 11767 of February 19, 1974 (39 FR 6603) consists of one operative paragraph designating the Organization of African Unity as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. Section 3 of EO 13377 of April 13, 2005 (70 FR 20263, published April 18, 2005) provides: "Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked." The order has no own-terms sunset, condition or report date. Searches of the held corpus for the order's number found only EO 13377, the order's own texts, and an eCFR list (8 CFR 316.20) that still names the OAU designation; none revokes, supersedes or amends it earlier. The current-law table (jobs/current-law/output/ORDERS_CURRENT_LAW.csv) records one U.S. Code mention (MENTIONS.csv row usc:c26b8d90ee04, the editorial note to 22 U.S.C. 288) that lists the Organization of African Unity designation by Executive Order No. 11767 and says it was revoked by Executive Order No. 13377, section 3, April 13, 2005 (70 F.R. 20263), which agrees with the end recorded here, and one eCFR mention (8 CFR 316.20, amended through 2026-10-14) in a list of organizations that still names the Organization of African Unity with this order's date. That regulatory list makes no designation of its own and does not purport to restore the order, so it is not a current predicate for it; it is a stale list entry disclosed as a lead. The first and only dated end is the revocation on April 13, 2005.

savings.reason: EO 13377 designates the African Union in section 1, preserves in section 2 only privileges the African Union may otherwise hold, and revokes EO 11767 in section 3 without any saving clause for the OAU designation. The single command of EO 11767 was the designation itself; no continuing independent command or accrued obligation is located in the held texts.
